newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKISH SHARES FIRMER AFTER CONFIDENCE VOTE.
newsitem.headline: TURKISH SHARES FIRMER AFTER CONFIDENCE VOTE.

text.p: Istanbul shares were firmer in quiet mid-morning trade on Monday following the Saturday confidence vote won by Turkey's new right-left coalition government headed by Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz.

The IMKB National-100 which brushed a new trading record of 2,044 in the first half of the session, stood at 2,043 at 0825 GMT, up 16 points, or 0.79 percent from Friday's all-time high close of 2,027.

"There were sales at the opening because market moving expectations came to an end with the confidence vote. The market may start buying on fresh expectations in coming days," said Niyazi Atasever from Genborsa securities.
"The trend will depend on the new government's performance," he added.

The index had surged 29.5 percent to Friday's all-time high from June 18 when the former Islamist-led coalition resigned and hopes flared that it would be replaced by a secularist alliance. It hit nine records during the three-ween-long rally.
